public_rationale: A June 25, 2026 preprint reports growing Codex use in the first half of 2026 [e1]. METR's February 24, 2026 update reports tentative developer speedups but says selection effects and unreliable time measurements limit the results [e2]. These studies establish neither sustained time savings comparable to major historical labor-saving technologies nor permanent impossibility of that outcome [e1, e2]. The forecast therefore remains unresolved.
limitations: The adoption evidence does not measure realized human time savings after supervision, checking, and correction [e1].
The developer study provides an unreliable estimate of productivity effects and no historical-scale comparison [e2].
“Eventually” supplies no deadline, and “among the biggest” supplies no numerical ranking [marcus-ai-agents-have-so-far-mostly-been-1e53ce-o1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI agents will not go away and will eventually be among the biggest time-savers humanity has known.

statement.excerpt: I don’t expect agents to go away; eventually AI agents will be among the biggest time-savers humanity has ever known.
statement.document_title: AI Agents have, so far, mostly been a dud

from_speaker: I don’t expect agents to go away
among the biggest time-savers humanity has ever known
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that agents will persist and eventually deliver widespread time savings comparable in importance and scale to history’s major labor-saving technologies.
The claim covers AI agents generally, without restricting their architecture to LLMs.
Time savings should account for human supervision, checking, and correction. Adoption and task performance alone do not establish time saved.
Eventually supplies no deadline. No finite period of disappointing results can by itself contradict this forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evidence establishes sustained adoption and realized human time savings at a scale comparable to history’s major labor-saving technologies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that agents permanently disappear or that the forecast’s eventual achievement is impossible. Temporary abandonment, modest savings, and unsuccessful current systems are insufficient.

evidence.explanation: METR reports tentative speedups but warns that participant selection and time measurement make the estimates unreliable. This narrow research does not establish or rule out eventual historical-scale savings.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Credible, dated evidence of persistent adoption and sustained human time savings, accounting for oversight and rework, comparable to major historical labor-saving technologies; or decisive evidence permanently precluding that outcome.
